name: Slosh
description: Slosh is a four-handed British domino game from the Trains family, played with a double-six set. The engine tile is placed in the center; each player has a train (a line of tiles) extending from the engine toward them. On your turn you add a tile to your own train if you can; if you cannot, the next player may slosh (play on your train) then play on their own. The round ends when someone dominoes or the game is blocked; lowest pip count in hand wins the round. Scoring is with poker chips or pencil.

history.origins: British member of the Trains family. The name refers to water or liquid spilling over (sloshing), evoking splashing someone at a bar.
history.cultural: British domino tradition; connecting cross layout.
history.evolution: Played with double-six set; four trains extend diagonally from the engine.

setup.players: Four players. A four-handed British domino game; each player has their own train extending from the center engine toward them, and play proceeds to the left.
setup.deck: Double-six domino set. Each player receives six tiles; four tiles form the boneyard and are not used in the round.
setup.dealing: Each player gets six tiles. The engine for the first round is the double-four; if it is in the boneyard, the hand is redealt until someone has it. The player with the engine places it first; play proceeds to the left.
setup.equipment: Double-six domino set, markers or poker chips (or pencil) for scoring.

rules.objective: Win rounds by dominoing (emptying your hand) or having the lowest pip count when the game is blocked. The lowest scorer is paid the difference by each other player.
rules.gameplay: The engine is placed in the center. Each player has a train extending from the engine toward them (traditionally the four trains extend diagonally from the four corners of the engine). On your turn, add a tile to your own train if you can, matching the open end. If you cannot play, the next player may slosh (play a tile on your train) before adding a tile to their own train. If the previous player could play on their train, you may only play on your own train. The round ends when someone dominoes or the game is blocked; hands are scored by pips left (domino scores zero).
keyRules: Engine for each round: double-four, then double-five, double-six, double-one, double-two, double-three.
Player with engine places it first; play to the left.
Add to own train if possible; if not, next player may slosh then play on own train.
Lowest pip count wins the round; domino scores zero; lowest is paid the difference by others.

strategy.basic: Watch your train and the one to your right; those are the only places you can play. Slosh as much as you can to get rid of tiles and domino before others.
strategy.intermediate: The four dead tiles in the boneyard make the game trickier; you can never be sure what tiles are in play. Count exposed tiles in each suit to know what is likely in the hand of the player to your left (who can slosh you).
strategy.advanced: If you do not have a protected suit, count tiles exposed in each suit and end your train with the most-played suit so the player to your left is less likely to have a match. If you are running out of plays on your own train, invite a slosh by getting the least-exposed suit on the end of your train to give yourself an opening.
tips: Start with double-four because there are four players.
Defensive play is harder; the rest of the board tells you what tiles are not yet played.

synthesis.shortDescription: Slosh is a four-handed British domino game (double-six set). Each player has a train from the center engine; on your turn add to your train or slosh on the right-hand opponent's train if they could not play.
